title: Aachen heat transition
description: Heating system turnover in Aachen's 3,660 inhabited Zensus 100 m cells, 2022–2045: Weibull replacement, logit choice of the new system, district heating gated by the adopted heat plan. Cell data is computed from the raw public downloads: Python decodes them, simple formulas sum them per cell.

census_heating_grid.description: Residential buildings by heating energy carrier for every inhabited 100 m cell in Germany.

heat_plan_blocks.description: Building blocks of the adopted heat plan with the heat supplied by each carrier in the target scenario for 2022, 2030, 2035, 2040 and 2045: q_<carrier>_<yy>, where fw is district and nw local heating.

source.locator: Layer app:kwp_baubloecke_join, properties q_fw_* (district heating) and q_nw_* (local heating)

source.assumption: Baseline: the NRW model's moderate renovation pathway
Unit conversion: one MWh is 1000 kWh

source.locator: Tables 3.3.1 and 3.3.2 (non-condensing oil and gas appliances by installation period, row "Summe"); 3.4.1 and 3.4.2 (condensing: oil 991,410 of which 984,420 built 2000–2025; gas 8,845,660 of which 8,607,290)
source.note: National figures for 2025; no Aachen or NRW breakdown is published. Other technologies are 0 here and get assumed ages instead.

source.assumption: Age in 2025 of each installation period: b0 = 2015–2025, b1 = 2005–2014, b2 = 1995–2004, b3 = before 1995. Condensing boilers from before 2000 go to b2; those from 2000–2025 are split 11:10:5 across b0, b1, b2, assuming equal installations per year.

No survey covers these technologies. Heat pumps are mostly recent, biomass boilers grew after 2005, night storage heaters are old, district heating connections and the rest are spread evenly. Gas and oil come from the chimney sweep survey.
Model design: ten-year age buckets
Model design: midpoint of each ten-year bucket

Characteristic lifetimes. Long for gas and oil because the chimney sweep survey finds about 66% of gas and over 86% of oil appliances older than 20 years; district heating stations and storage heaters rarely fail.
Shape 3: failure rates rise with age, as is common for wear-out of heating equipment

Household end-user prices per MWh of final energy, excluding the CO₂ price: the 2022 crisis peak, 2025 levels, then gently falling electricity (heat pump tariff below the household tariff). District heating is priced through the network instead.

2022–2026 follow the statutory BEHG prices (§ 10: 30, 30, 45, 55 EUR/t, and the 55–65 EUR/t corridor for 2026, upper bound taken). From 2027 heating fuels move to the EU ETS2, whose price is not set: 100 EUR/t by 2030 and 200 EUR/t by 2045 are assumptions.
Fuel emission factors for natural gas and heating oil, as used for BEHG pricing; other carriers are outside the BEHG price on heating

source.locator: § 43 (1): minimum share of biomethane or bio-oil for new gas and oil heating – 10% from 2029, 15% from 2030, 30% from 2035, 60% from 2040
source.note: The model applies the current year's quota to the cost of a newly chosen boiler (myopic owners).

source.locator: § 43 (1) applies to heating systems fired with gaseous or liquid fuels

source.assumption: End-user price of biomethane and bio-oil (no CO₂ price); only used where the quota applies
Annual efficiency of the appliance; heat pumps use the cell's seasonal performance factor instead (0 here is unused)
Definition: only heat pumps convert with the seasonal performance factor
Annualised installation cost per MWh of heat for a typical single-family house, after subsidies
Definition: only district heating needs the network
Definition: the technologies a fossil heating ban would exclude
Night storage heaters, coal and unheated buildings are kept in the stock but no longer chosen for new installations

source.locator: The Gebäudemodernisierungsgesetz removes the requirement that new heating systems run on at least 65% renewable energy (§§ 71–73 GEG 2024)
source.note: 9999 encodes that no fossil ban applies; the Bio-Treppe in bio_quota replaces it.

source.assumption: Cost sensitivity of the logit choice: a 10 EUR/MWh cost difference shifts the odds by about a quarter
Preferences beyond cost: oil tank and biomass storage space, heat pump hassle; gas and district heating are the reference
Baseline: network expansion on the heat plan's schedule
Distribution network cost per metre of street, uniform across cells
Real discount rate of a municipal utility
Network depreciation period
Connection rate the utility prices with in a new area; avoids division by zero
Heat generation and operation cost of the network, excluding pipes

nodes.label: Buildings of the NRW model
nodes.description: Decodes the base layer of the NRW heat demand model straight out of the zip: one row per heated building.

buildings.description: Heated buildings (beheizt = 1) of layer WBM-NRW, with the columns the model uses.

id.description: Fest_ID: the building's id in every layer of the NRW model

cell.description: Raster_ID: the 100 m census cell the building stands in

demand_kwh.description: RW_WW: space heating and hot water demand today

spf_air.description: JAZ_Luft: estimated seasonal performance factor of an air-source heat pump

heat_line.description: WLD_ID: the heat line (street segment) serving the building

location.description: Centre of the footprint's bounding box

nodes.label: Demand under renovation pathways
nodes.description: Decodes the three renovation layers of the NRW model for the heated buildings.

building_projections.description: Space heating and hot water demand per heated building in kWh/year, one column <pathway>_<year> per renovation pathway and year: 2022 is the base model, later years the pathway's projection (layers WBM-NRW-moderat/erhoeht/hoch, columns RW_WW_<m|e|h>_<yy>). Buildings without a projection keep their 2022 demand.

cell.description: Raster_ID: the 100 m census cell the building stands in

nodes.label: Heat lines of the NRW model
nodes.description: Decodes the heat line layer: street segments with heat demand.

street_length.description: Strassenla: length of the street segment

nodes.label: Census heating carriers in Aachen
nodes.description: Streams the nationwide census grid and keeps the cells that hold heated buildings of the NRW model.

census_cells.description: Residential buildings per 100 m cell by heating energy carrier, as published; "–" reads as 0 as the census documentation prescribes.

cell.description: GITTER_ID_100m in the NRW model's Raster_ID notation

nodes.label: Cells of the model
nodes.description: Keeps the census cells that have heating counts and at least one heated residential building: the 3,660 cells the model runs on.

cells.description: Cells with census counts and at least one heated residential building in the NRW model.

nodes.label: Heating stock per cell
nodes.description: Counts the residential buildings of each cell by heating technology in 2022, from the census heating carriers.

heating_stock.description: Census buildings per cell and heating energy carrier, mapped to seven technologies. Category counts and cell totals are perturbed independently by the census, so the model uses the categories.

nodes.label: Heat demand per cell
nodes.description: Sums the heat demand of the buildings in each cell, today and under each renovation pathway.

heat_demand.description: Space heating and hot water demand of every heated building, summed per cell (building Raster_ID = census cell id). 2022 is the base model; 2025–2045 are the model's projections for each renovation pathway.

nodes.label: Street length per cell
nodes.description: Splits the length of streets with heat demand among the cells their buildings stand in.

street_length.description: Length of the model's heat line segments (streets with heat demand), each split among cells in proportion to the demand of the buildings it serves.

nodes.label: Heat pump performance per cell
nodes.description: How efficiently an air-source heat pump would run in each cell, weighted by the demand of its buildings.

heat_pump_spf.description: Demand-weighted mean of the model's air-source heat pump seasonal performance factor (JAZ_Luft) over the residential buildings of each cell.

nodes.label: Buildings in heat plan blocks
nodes.description: Point-in-polygon join of the building centres with the heat plan block outlines, in EPSG:25832.

building_blocks.description: Each heated building's heat plan block; buildings outside every block have none.

first_network_year.description: First plan year (2022, 2030, 2035, 2040, 2045) in which the block is supplied by district or local heating; 2100 means never

nodes.label: Network year per cell
nodes.description: The first year the heat plan brings district or local heating to most of each cell's demand.

dh_expansion_year.description: The first plan year by which blocks holding at least half of the cell's demand are supplied by district or local heating; 2100 means not planned.

nodes.label: Heat plan network share
nodes.description: The share of heat the adopted heat plan expects district and local heating to supply in each target year.

heat_plan_network_share.value: sum(total(q_fw_{year}, q_nw_{year})) / sum(total(q_bhkw_{year}, q_biom_{year}, q_el_{year}, q_fw_{year}, q_gas_{year}, q_gwp_{year}, q_h2_{year}, q_lng_{year}, q_lwp_{year}, q_nw_{year}, q_oel_{year}, q_stc_{year}))
heat_plan_network_share.description: District plus local heating supply divided by the supply of all twelve carriers, over all heat plan blocks, per target year. Blocks without a value for a carrier count as zero.

nodes.label: Renovation pathway
nodes.description: Picks the heat demand of the renovation pathway the scenario assumes.

nodes.label: Linear heat density
nodes.description: Heat demand per metre of street: whether a district heating network would pay off in the cell.

nodes.label: Initial age structure
nodes.description: Survey counts by period, bucketed; technologies without survey data use the assumed weights.

nodes.label: Weibull replacement hazard
nodes.description: How likely a heating system of each age is to be replaced in a year, from a Weibull lifetime.

nodes.label: Energy cost per MWh of heat
nodes.description: Fuel blended with the mandatory biogenic share, plus CO₂ price, divided by efficiency or the cell's heat pump performance.

energy_cost.equation: ((1 - bio_quota * quota_applies) * (fuel_price + co2_price * emission_factor) + bio_quota * quota_applies * bio_fuel_price) / (uses_spf * spf + (1 - uses_spf) * efficiency)

nodes.label: Heating stock turnover
nodes.description: Ages each cell's heating systems, replaces those that fail, and lets owners choose the new system by annual cost, with district heating only where the network has arrived.

nodes.label: Heat plan target check
nodes.description: Compares the simulated district heating share with the share the heat plan targets.

groups.label: Buildings and cells
groups.description: Who is in the model: Aachen's heated buildings and the census cells they stand in. Decoded from the NRW heat demand model and the census grid by Python scripts in Pyodide.

groups.label: Today's heating
groups.description: What heats each cell today, how old the systems are, and how likely they are to be replaced as they age.

groups.label: Heat demand
groups.description: How much heat each cell needs, today and as buildings are renovated along the scenario's pathway.

groups.label: District heating reach
groups.description: Where and when district heating arrives under the heat plan, and whether a street has enough demand to pay for the pipes.

groups.label: Running costs
groups.description: What a MWh of heat costs with each system in each cell: fuel, CO₂ price, the biogenic quota and the system's efficiency.

groups.label: Replacement choices
groups.description: Systems wear out and owners pick their replacement by annual cost, 2022–2045: the stock-and-flow model at the heart of the pipeline.

groups.label: Heat plan check
groups.description: Does district heating reach the share the adopted heat plan targets?
